item.title: Two more Chittagong port terminals set to go to foreign operators
item.description:
Following the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), the process of handing over the operational responsibilities of the Chittagong Container Terminal (CCT), General Cargo Berth (GCB) and Bay Port Multipurpose Terminal to foreign operators has begun.
The Ministry of Shipping has directed the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) to initiate the process of appointing Saudi Arabia-based Red Sea Gateway Terminal International (RSGTI) to operate the CCT. The directive was issued on September 28.
The CCT is currently operated by local private firm Saif Powertec Limited, while the GCB is managed by the Chittagong Port Authority.
Meanwhile, the Port Protection Committee has demanded cancellation of the proposed 15-year concession agreement with a foreign operator for the NCT and its overflow container yard. The committee has also called for an end to plans to hand over the NCT and CCT to foreign operators.
The committee announced that it would stage a daylong sit-in at the main gate of Chittagong Port on Monday if its demands are not met.
The demands were announced at a press conference at the Chittagong Press Club auditorium on Saturday.
Committee representatives said that if the government does not clearly announce by October 5 that the initiatives to hand over the NCT and CCT will be cancelled, they will announce further programmes as part of a broader movement.
A letter signed by Farzana Hossain, senior assistant secretary of the Ministry of Shipping, on September 28 said the Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL), the advisory body, had been requested to process the appointment letter for RSGTI as the operator of the CCT.
The letter said RSGTI had expressed interest in implementing the Chittagong Port Authority’s CCT and GCB and Bay Port Multipurpose Terminal projects under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
It also referred to a letter issued by the PPP Authority on August 19, 2016, and directed that further action be taken after considering the matter.
Dubai-based terminal operator DP World and RSGTI separately submitted proposals on April 8 and April 22 to operate the CCT. Local conglomerate MGH Group also submitted a proposal.
RSGTI has also expressed interest in operating the GCB alongside the CCT. The company said it plans to invest around $1 billion if selected.
In 2025, around 16% of Chittagong Port’s total container traffic was handled through the CCT. The NCT handled around 44%, the GCB 36% and the Patenga Container Terminal (PCT) 4%.
The government has also granted in-principle approval to a draft agreement to hand over the operation and maintenance of the NCT and its Overflow Container Yard (OCY) to an international terminal operator for 15 years.
The approval was given at a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on October 1 based on a proposal from the Ministry of Shipping.
The project, titled “Operation and Maintenance of the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) and Overflow Yard (OCY) of the Chittagong Port Authority”, is being implemented under a PPP framework.
According to data from the PPP Authority, the Chittagong Port Authority plans to entrust the modernisation, operation and maintenance of the NCT to Dubai-based DP World under a government-to-government agreement.
The project received initial in-principle approval from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on March 23, 2023.
The NCT is currently operated by Chittagong Dry Dock Company Limited, which is owned by the Bangladesh Navy. The terminal handles around 1.3 million TEUs annually, accounting for about 40% of Chittagong Port’s total container traffic.
Four container terminals are currently operational at Chittagong Port: the NCT, CCT, GCB and PCT.
The NCT is operated by Navy-owned Chittagong Dry Dock Company Limited, while the CCT is operated by Saif Powertec. The GCB is managed by the port authority.
The PCT is operated by Saudi Arabia-based RSGTI, which began operating the terminal under a 22-year agreement in 2024.
Fazlul Kabir Mintu, member secretary of the Port Protection Committee, told Bangla Tribune that Chittagong Port was nationally vital infrastructure directly linked to the country’s foreign trade, imports and exports, revenue generation, commerce and industry.
“I have learned that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, during its meeting on October 1, granted in-principle approval to the draft of a 15-year concession agreement with an international operator for the operation and maintenance of the NCT and the overflow yard,” he said.
He said handing over the NCT under a 15-year concession was not merely a routine administrative or commercial decision.
“Before finalising such a move, a comprehensive and transparent comparative assessment needs to be made public, covering projected revenue under state management, capacity enhancement, adoption of modern technology and automation, and skill development, alongside the potential financial benefits to the state if the concession is granted,” he added.
When contacted, Syed Refayet Hamim, secretary of the Chittagong Port Authority, declined to comment on the proposed handover of the NCT or any other terminal.

item.title: Police seeks to keep Akhtaruzzaman in jail over airport incident
item.description:
Police have sought to keep former MP Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman in jail following allegations that he created a disturbance over a shortage of luggage trolleys at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, obstructed official duties and assaulted an on-duty security official.
Sub-Inspector Majedul Islam of Airport police station, also the investigating officer in the case, confirmed the matter on Sunday afternoon.
“After the remand period ended, we produced him before the court and applied to have him detained in jail,” he said.
SI Abu Bakkar Siddique of the prosecution division said a hearing on the matter is scheduled at the Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Court.
On Saturday, the court granted Akhtaruzzaman one day’s remand for questioning.
Earlier on Friday evening, the Detective Branch (DB) arrested him from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area.
A video circulated on social media earlier showed Akhtaruzzaman raising his voice over a delay in distributing Zamzam water to Umrah pilgrims who had arrived from Medina on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight on Thursday morning.
In the video, the former MP is seen addressing airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad and threatening to throw him out of the airport while accusing him of securing his position through lobbying.
According to the case statement, 34 Jamaat-e-Islami representatives, accompanied by their families, arrived at Dhaka Airport from Medina on Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-338 at 8:55am on Thursday.
Due to a heavy influx of arriving passengers, long queues formed for luggage trolleys. Several protocol assistants allegedly attempted to bypass the queue to secure trolleys.
The situation became tense over delays in receiving luggage and Zamzam water, the case statement said.
Around 10:45am, Dhaka-5 MP Mohammad Kamal Hossain summoned the airport executive director to the scene.
The executive director arrived and began speaking with those concerned. At that point, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly approached him aggressively and verbally abused him.
The case statement said the executive director tried to explain the situation regarding the surge of passengers and trolley management, but Akhtaruzzaman became increasingly agitated and allegedly threatened him.
Fearing further escalation, MP Kamal Hossain moved the executive director to a safe distance, according to the complaint.
The complaint further alleges that Akhtaruzzaman later threatened those present and made derogatory remarks about Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat.
Several protocol assistants accompanying Akhtaruzzaman allegedly recorded the incident and threatened to circulate the footage on social media.
According to the case details, security supervisor Mohammad Kamal Uddin instructed those involved not to record videos in the airport’s Key Point Installation (KPI) area, citing security concerns.
Akhtaruzzaman allegedly approached Warrant Officer Kamal Uddin, verbally abused him and assaulted him.
The FIR said the alleged assault was not captured on CCTV but could be corroborated by the victim and eyewitnesses.
A Biman Bangladesh Airlines representative later arrived at the scene, and Akhtaruzzaman allegedly behaved aggressively towards him as well.
The case statement also alleges that Akhtaruzzaman threw bottles of Zamzam water belonging to passengers from a trolley.
Akhtaruzzaman, a former MP for the Kishoreganj-2 constituency, joined Jamaat-e-Islami ahead of the 13th parliamentary election.
He previously won the Katiadi constituency as a BNP candidate in 1991 and June 1996.
In the recent election, his younger brother Anisuzzaman Khokon, a former BNP MP for Mymensingh-19, contested the same seat as an independent candidate.
Meanwhile, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has temporarily suspended two officials over the delay in distributing Zamzam water to Umrah pilgrims.
The officials are Baggage In-charge Monirul Islam Prodhan and Flight Supervisor Saddam Hossain.
They have also been asked to explain allegations of negligence in their duties.

item.title: Bangladesh condemns Houthi drone attack on power plant in Medina
item.description:
Bangladesh has strongly condemned a Houthi drone attack on the Taibah power plant in Medina, Saudi Arabia.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement on Sunday expressing Bangladesh’s condemnation of the attack.
The statement said the deliberate targeting of critical civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque (Al-Masjid an-Nabawi) was an unacceptable assault on the sanctity of one of Islam’s holiest sites.
Bangladesh expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its security and sovereignty.
It also reaffirmed its opposition to acts of aggression that undermine regional peace and stability.

item.title: Leave small businesses alone
item.description:
There's a good argument that every business in the country should be registered -- so that we know who is doing what, who is obeying tax laws, and so on.
There's also a good argument for keeping really small businesses completely out of the bureaucratic system -- for really small businesses simply do not have the time, or often even the knowledge, to be able to deal with the bureaucracy.
As is obvious, these two arguments are in conflict with each other.
The correct error -- or at least I would insist, which is not quite the same thing as insisting I am correct to do so -- is to be on the side of allowing small businesses to escape the bureaucracy.
This is the background to the requirement that every business must now have a BIN -- a Business Identification Number.
The claim is that this requirement hits cottage, micro, small, and medium enterprises (CMSMEs) hard. It isn't that applying for the number is difficult. It's that it can be difficult to get the supporting documentation required to be able to make that application.
For example, a legal rental agreement -- or property deed - is required for the business address. Yet plenty of micro businesses run from the left hand side of the family dining table.
If we're talking about manufacturing, then it requires a machinery list, an equipment layout plan, and input-output coefficient information. There are people out there running perfectly fine businesses who don't know what that last part means, and I'm not sure I do either.
It's obvious what is happening here. The bureaucracy thinks it would be a fine thing if everyone in business were doing business correctly and in a formal and registered manner.
Thus they can use the need for a BIN to make sure that everyone is indeed doing things correctly -- working at a property licensed to run a business from, for example. For larger businesses, this could even be true too.
For smaller businesses -- micro, cottage, and so on -- these requirements can be the difference between it being worth being a legal business at all or remaining in the shadows of the grey economy.
Grey here meaning not illegal as a business -- that's the black economy. Just one that's not registered and paying taxes and such.
And here's the thing. We all want to have economic growth. That's how to climb that ladder from a less developed economy all the way up to a developed and rich one.
Economic growth comes from new business formation. Very little of total economic growth comes from large companies growing yet more.
Nearly all of it comes from someone using that corner of the kitchen table to come up with a new idea and trying it out.
Barriers to those tryouts limit, slow, or even stop, economic growth.
The correct answer, therefore, is to reverse that process of applying for the legality of the business.
Get people signed up for the BIN first. Say, if you have some form of personal ID, then you can apply online for that BIN.
Great, you're now a business and you can use that number to gain access to a bank account and all the rest.
We can worry about obeying all of the other laws -- when you need to provide a machinery layout plan, for example -- to when you're a large enough business that it's worth worrying about.
Yes, some people will abuse this reversal of the current process. But that's just the same argument as we started with.
It would be good if everyone was running every business according to all the rules. But the rules also prevent some people from starting up in business at all.
The error should be, again to my mind, on getting the business happening first -- for that's the part that makes us richer -- and worrying about compliance with all the bureaucratic laws later.
Adam Smith pointed out that the only things required to move from barbarism to the highest degree of opulence is peace, easy taxes, and the tolerable administration of justice.
That “tolerable” there means yes, of course everyone absolutely must obey the really important laws but a certain benign neglect of the details is also necessary.
Or even, as we can and should put it, less bureaucracy means more business. Let's err on the side of more business as that's the one that makes us richer.
Tim Worstall is a senior fellow at Adam Smith.

item.title: Your phone number is now your identity. Guard it
item.description:
A shopkeeper in Mirpur comes home from Friday prayers and sees that his phone has no signal. He blames the network, as most of us would. By the time he gets to a service centre the next morning, his mobile wallet is empty, he's locked out of Facebook, and three of his cousins have received messages from "him" asking for money.
The shopkeeper is invented, but the sequence is a familiar one. And none of it took clever hacking. Whoever did this only needed his number.
It's worth stopping to think about how much a Bangladeshi phone number carries these days. It receives the one-time password for your wallet. It's how you get back into Facebook when you forget your password, how WhatsApp knows it's you, how the courier confirms your parcel.
Banks lean on it more every year. We built one of the most phone-dependent economies anywhere, and somewhere along the way, 11 digits became the key to nearly everything. Nobody planned it. It just happened.
Attackers noticed long before users did. In my years running security work in Silicon Valley, I saw them go after whatever opened the most doors, again and again. Here, that's the SIM.
Most of the time they don't even have to take it, because we hand it over.
Someone calls, says he's from your wallet provider, warns that your account will be suspended, and asks you to read out the code you've just received.
Or a message arrives: Sorry, I sent my code to your number by mistake, could you forward it?
These tricks work because Bangladeshis are, on the whole, helpful people who trust a polite voice.
A real provider will never ask for your PIN or OTP. Not by phone, not by SMS, and not through a relative who says the company told them to.
When a fraudster can't talk the code out of you, he may go after the SIM itself and get a replacement issued in your name.
Biometric SIM registration made that much harder. I worked on those systems, and it was a real step forward that many wealthier countries still haven't taken.
It didn't make it impossible, though. Forged papers, a bribed insider, or a careless recovery process can still get someone through.
What you'd notice is your phone going dead while everyone around you still has signal. Most people wait a day before dealing with that, and a day is more than enough.
Then there are the apps: A cracked game, an "update" someone forwarded on WhatsApp, a free copy of something that normally costs money.
Some of these ask to read your SMS, or to use Android's accessibility features, which were built for people with disabilities and let an app see and tap whatever is on your screen.
Say yes, and the app can read your OTPs as they arrive. You never share anything. It simply watches.
Start with the OTP. Treat it like cash, and don't give it to anyone, including someone who sounds exactly like a family member.
Put a PIN on WhatsApp through their two-step verification settings, which takes about two minutes.
If your signal drops for no obvious reason, call your operator from someone else's phone within the hour, and let your wallet provider know too.
Get your apps from the Play Store, and when a torch app asks to read your messages, ask yourself why.
Finally, have one conversation at home about a family code word, something only you would know, to ask for whenever money comes up. It sounds like something out of a movie, but it costs nothing and it works.
Still, it isn't fair to leave all of this to individuals. A phone number was never meant to prove who someone is on its own.
In several countries, banks and mobile operators have started passing each other one simple piece of information: Has this SIM been replaced in the past few days? If it has, the large transfer waits until someone checks.
Bangladesh has already done the hard part with biometric registration, so it could do this more easily than most.
The same thinking applies inside the phone. Security that catches a malicious app before it gets anywhere near a wallet or banking app should come as standard, rather than something people discover after they've been robbed.
October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month. We tend to measure how digital Bangladesh is by how many people are online. A better measure might be how many of them feel safe once they get there.
Everyone who loses money this way tells their family, their neighbours, the regulars at the tea stall. Each story makes the next person a little warier of going digital, and that wariness takes a long time to wear off.
The number is already our identity. We just haven't started treating it that way.
Zeeshan R Khan led a security practice at Cisco for more than 12 years and is based in Silicon Valley. He is the founder of SurroundApps, which builds mobile security and family-safety technology for Bangladesh.

item.title: 54 health ministry officials assigned to monitor hospital services
item.description:
The Health and Family Welfare Ministry has assigned 54 officials to inspect and monitor hospitals across the country to improve the quality of healthcare services, maintain administrative discipline and ensure better public service.
An office order issued by the Administration-1 branch of the Health Services Division on September 30 assigned the officials to inspect medical colleges, specialised, general, district and upazila-level hospitals across the country.
According to the order, additional secretaries, joint secretaries and deputy secretaries have been assigned to monitor specific hospitals as well as hospitals across different districts and divisions. Some officials have also been given additional responsibility for hospitals in other districts.
The officials have been instructed to coordinate with hospital authorities and take necessary measures to improve healthcare services, including monitoring manpower, cleanliness, medical equipment, infrastructure, security and overall management at hospitals under their jurisdiction.
They will also regularly monitor the digital attendance of doctors and healthcare workers and submit attendance-related information and reports to the relevant authorities.
The officials have been asked to coordinate with deputy commissioners, civil surgeons, upazila nirbahi officers and upazila health and family welfare officers to monitor the progress of vaccination programmes, infectious disease prevention and public awareness activities.
The order also directs them to participate in and provide necessary support for public health initiatives, including maternal and child healthcare, elderly healthcare and nutrition programmes.
They have also been instructed to encourage healthcare institutions to undertake innovative and effective initiatives to improve service quality and provide necessary support for their implementation.
The officials must regularly visit districts, upazilas and hospitals under their jurisdiction. During inspections, they are required to discuss identified problems, observations and recommendations with relevant authorities and take necessary steps to implement feasible recommendations.
Based on observations and recommendations from each inspection, the officials must prepare reports and submit them to the designated branch by the 7th of every month.
Each official is required to conduct at least one inspection every month.
According to the list attached to the office order, additional secretaries from various branches, including administration, development, global health, hospitals, public health, finance and audit, budget and nursing, have been assigned to monitor major national hospitals and hospitals in different divisions.
Among the institutions assigned to specific monitoring officials are Dhaka Medical College Hospital, Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, Sir Salimullah Medical College and Mitford Hospital, Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital, National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, National Institute of Mental Health and National Institute of Ophthalmology and Hospital.
Joint secretaries and deputy secretaries have been assigned to monitor hospitals in different districts. Their responsibilities include monitoring district-level hospitals as well as, in many cases, upazila-level facilities.
The officials have been instructed to coordinate with the district administration, health authorities and hospital authorities while carrying out their duties.
The initiative aims to identify existing problems at hospitals through regular inspections, take steps to address them and monitor the progress of healthcare services.
The order said the assigned responsibilities would be additional to the officials’ regular duties and would take effect from the date of issuance.
The initiative is expected to enable the ministry to obtain regular information on the ground realities of healthcare services, staff attendance, use of medical equipment, infrastructure problems and management gaps through direct inspections by central-level officials. It could also facilitate quicker action based on inspection reports.

item.title: Three associates of local teenage gang leader arrested in Ctg
item.description:
Police have arrested three people, including a woman, allegedly associated with local teenage gang leader Wakil Hossain Boga, during a raid in the Jalalabad area under Khulshi police station in Chittagong.
The three were arrested on Saturday night based on a tip-off, police said.
The arrestees are Abdul Hannan, Monir Hossain, alias Emon, and Sabiha Begum. Police said five to six cases are pending against Hannan and Emon.
According to police, Wakil Hossain Boga, an expelled former joint convener of the city unit of Swechchhasebak Dal, controls several teenage gangs and faces at least 16 criminal cases.
Recently, a clash took place between the "Seven Star" gang, allegedly controlled by Wakil, and a rival group known as "Five Star". A teenager, Mohammad Hridoy, was killed in the clash.
Abdur Rahim, officer-in-charge of Khulshi police station, said the three associates of Wakil were arrested during a raid based on secret information.
They will be produced before the court, he added.

item.title: Sullivan becomes youngest US goalscorer in 3-0 rout of Mexico
item.description:
Cavan Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in United States history at just 17 years and five days as the USA swept arch-rivals Mexico aside 3-0 in a friendly international in Arizona on Sunday.
Sullivan, who is set to join English Premier League side Manchester City next year, doubled the hosts’ lead with a superbly taken goal in the 62nd minute at State Farm Stadium in Glendale.
The teenager surpassed Mathis Albert’s record as the youngest US international goalscorer. Albert, aged 17 years and 31 days, had set the mark only five days earlier when he scored in the USA’s 4-2 win over Chile.
“These are the moments you dream of when you’re three, four, five or six-year-old,” Sullivan said.
“I manifested this moment, not just these past couple of hours when I found out I was starting, but my whole life.”
Sullivan’s landmark goal came after another teenager, 18-year-old Julian Hall, had put Mauricio Pochettino’s side ahead in the 28th minute.
Hall has now scored in each of his last three international appearances since making his debut under Pochettino in last week’s defeat of Peru. He also found the net in the win over Chile.
The USA made the most of their chances despite Mexico controlling much of the possession and territory in the opening stages.
Hall opened the scoring with a close-range finish after Gio Reyna burst into the penalty area to collect a pass from Alex Freeman before beating Mexico midfielder Erik Lira and reaching the byline.
Reyna’s low cross was parried by Mexico goalkeeper Raul Rangel, but only as far as Hall, who lashed the rebound into the net.
Mexico came close to an equaliser early in the second half when Roberto Alvarado’s powerful effort from the edge of the area was tipped over by US goalkeeper Diego Kochen.
But Sullivan then produced the moment that made history.
The forward chased down a long ball after Rangel mishit a pass outside his area, took control and calmly chipped the goalkeeper from distance to make it 2-0.
“I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn't hit the crossbar or go over,” Sullivan said. “I was getting nervous when it was in the air and then everything was a blur.”
Mexico’s night deteriorated further when substitute Luis Chavez was sent off in the 68th minute for putting a hand in the face of Sebastian Berhalter.
The USA added a third in the 84th minute when Malik Tillman pounced on a poor Mexico backpass and fired into the top corner.

item.title: Fernandes hails Portugal's 'greatest symbol' Ronaldo, calls for unity
item.description:
Portugal playmaker Bruno Fernandes said Cristiano Ronaldo remains the country's greatest footballing icon despite walking out on the squad this week after finding out he would not start a match.
The 41-year-old superstar said Wednesday he had left the team after coach Jorge Jesus said Ronaldo would not start against Denmark in the Nations League, a match Portugal won 4-2 without him.
Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo's future with the national team, for whom he is the leading goalscorer and most capped player, is in doubt after his walk out.
"Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him, and what I told him, and what I repeat here, is this -- the most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world," Fernandes told reporters Saturday.
Manchester United midfielder Fernandes called for unity after a tumultuous few days in which Portugal fans' opinions have been split over Ronaldo's decision.
"He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things," said Fernandes.
"There are no divisions in the national team, it is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside...
"We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides, but, at the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone's respect, regardless of who likes him more or (who likes him) less."
Portugal beat Norway and Denmark away from home without Ronaldo starting and face Norway again on Sunday.
Coach Jesus said Ronaldo was a "symbol of Portugal" and said there would be time to speak about him after Sunday's game in Porto.
"I'm going to focus on the team, on the opponent which is Norway, one of the five best teams in Europe. That's the problem right now," said the 72-year-old coach.

item.title: Pretorius smashes Gayle's T20 record score
item.description:
Lhuan-dre Pretorius hit 188 not out off 79 deliveries in Bloemfontein to break Chris Gayle's record score in the T20 format.
Playing for the Titans against the Knights in the South African CSA Challenge, the 20-year-old left hander opened the batting and hit 13 sixes and 14 fours in his innings to surpass Gayle's 175 for Bengaluru in the Indian Premier League in 2013.
Pretorius reached 50 in 24 balls, needed 16 more to get to his century and took another 18 to hit 150.
Gayle scored his 175 off 66 balls striking 17 sixes and 13 fours.
The 20-year-old has represented South Africa in all three international formats. He was making his first Titans appearance of the season after scoring 226 total runs, tied for most with Dewald Brevis, in a three-nation series in Namibia in September.
On Friday, he dominated the strike, facing the equivalent of more than 13 overs to tie Australians Aaron Finch and Marcus Stoinis for the most balls faced in a T20 innings.
The second-highest scorer was Sinethemba Qeshile with 14 as the Titans finished on 267-3.
They then bowled out the Knights for 143 to win by 124 runs.
The Titans total was the second-highest in the competition's history, behind their 271 also against the Kings in 2022. In that match, Brevis hit 162, until Friday a competition record. This time he made seven.
The Cricinfo web site calculated that in 91 T20 games, Pretorius has a strike-rate of 150.44.

item.title: Liton rejects resignation calls after Bangladesh’s Asian Games failure
item.description:
Bangladesh captain Liton Das has ruled out resigning from the captaincy after the team’s Asian Games campaign ended without a medal.
He acknowledged that his own performance and the team’s overall cricket were below the standard.
Bangladesh had arrived at the Games with a medal target but lost to Pakistan before suffering another heavy defeat by Sri Lanka, which ended their campaign without a podium finish.
Asked whether he felt responsible for the failures and whether he would resign, Liton said he had not performed well in either match but saw no reason to step down.
“My performance was not up to the mark. I could not perform well in both matches,” Liton said at the post-match press conference.
But when asked directly if he wanted to resign, he replied: “No, I don’t want to resign. There are ups and downs in cricket. One day will be good, one day will be bad. There is nothing to resign for.”
Liton made two runs in Bangladesh’s first match and was dismissed for a duck against Sri Lanka.
He also accepted that Bangladesh had failed to make the most of an opportunity at the Asian Games.
“It is very bad,” he said. “We came here with a big target. When that did not happen, there was another option. We had an opportunity, but we missed it. We could not play good cricket, that’s why we missed the opportunities.”
Bangladesh’s captain said the team’s bowling had initially put them in a good position against Sri Lanka before an opposing batter produced an exceptional innings that changed the game.
“We bowled very well in the first eight overs,” Liton said. “Then you saw how a batter played shots on this wicket. It was very difficult, but he batted extraordinarily. Our bowlers did not get any clue about how to come back.”
The batting, he said, was not good enough to recover from the situation.
“Batting-wise, we were not up to the mark today,” Liton said.
The result means Bangladesh leave the Asian Games without the medal they had hoped to win through cricket.
Liton said the disappointment was natural for both the team and himself as captain.
“When you come from the country with a big target and cannot deliver that as a team, as a captain, everyone will feel bad,” he said. “Feeling bad is natural.”

item.title: World No.1 Rybakina ousted by world No. 118 in China Open second round
item.description:
World No.1 Elena Rybakina could not regroup and fell to 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva in the second round of the China Open on Saturday in Beijing.
The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan was playing her first match since seizing the top ranking on her US Open win in New York, but Armenia's Charaeva triumphed 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in a clinical comeback.
"I don't have words," said Charaeva, who is making her Beijing debut.
"This is incredible," the 24-year-old said.
"She's (an) amazing player, and for me it's kind of just dream come true," she said of Rybakina.
"I will be really happy to stay some more days in Beijing," she added. "Never stop believing, I guess."
Rybakina got off to a solid start, but seven double-faults ushered the momentum into the hands of her opponent.
Wind rattled the closed-roof stadium, with both players serving as thunderous claps echoed over the court.
A supportive crowd tried to rally Rybakina back into contention, but Charaeva held serve to win the match in two hours and 11 minutes.
Charaeva faces Briton Sonay Kartal in the third round.

item.title: Brazil shine on Selecao's first visit to India
item.description:
Five-time World Cup winners Brazil showed glimpses of their class in a 4-0 win over India in a rare football friendly between the two nations in Kolkata on Saturday.
India's hosting of a senior men's Brazil team for the first time had created buzz but a half-empty 65,000-capacity Salt Lake Stadium greeted the players.
Critics blamed the pricing of tickets for the low attendance despite Brazil's top stars including Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior and Marquinhos in the line-up.
The cheapest tickets were priced at 999 rupees ($10) but they were sold minutes after going on sale, while the next categories ranged between 3,500 and 25,000 rupees.
India, ranked 138th in the world, are looking to raise the profile of the sport in a cricket-mad country of 1.4 billion people.
Although the men's teams of the two countries were playing each other for the first time, the women's sides faced off in the Brazilian city of Manaus in 2021.
Brazil dominated play with Vinicius denied by a brave save from Indian goalkeeper and captain Gurpreet Singh Sandhu as early as the eighth minute.
India's forward line had a few good runs at the opposition goal, before Chelsea forward Estevao put Brazil ahead in the 28th minute with a quick left-foot shot that beat Gurpreet.
The goal rattled India's strategy and defence as Pedro doubled the lead in the 42nd minute.
"These (young) players played extremely well. They have improved on a day-to-day basis, starting from Australia to coming here," Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti said on his team's up and coming talent.
"They had an opportunity to showcase all of their qualities. They have done well and shown their talent even in difficult moments."
Brazil, who came to India off the back of a win and a draw in a friendly double-header in Australia, are looking to rebuild following their shock exit to Norway at the World Cup in July.
Brazil's yellow jerseys dominated the stands and Ancelotti's team did not disappoint with their smooth play.
Every Indian move was cheered by a raucous home crowd and Manvir Singh raised the volume when his powerful strike in the 55th minute drew a fine save.
Samuel Lino came off the bench in the second half in place of Vinicius and drilled in a third for Brazil in the 58th minute to make India pay for sloppy defending.
"Two or three goals were very soft due to individual errors. Our concentration was lacking at times," India coach Khalid Jamil told reporters.
"But players had belief and that is why they tried to play well. They should continue like this. Mentally we have to be strong."
"There was pressure, no doubt, on playing a champion side and we could not hide that," Jamil added.
Lino scored his second just before the final whistle to make it 4-0.
India have never qualified for a World Cup, and football, while popular, plays second fiddle to cricket.

item.title: Dhaka ranks world's third most polluted city Sunday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked as the world's third most polluted city on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 177 at 9:15am.
The air quality was classified in the "unhealthy" category, indicating that the concentration of airborne pollutants had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general public, according to the AQI scale.
India's capital Delhi topped the list with an AQI score of 235, followed by Kolkata with a score of 186. Indonesia's capital Jakarta, ranked fourth with an AQI score of 174.
An AQI reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy". Readings between 201 and 300 are deemed "very unhealthy", and levels above 301 are considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI, an index that tracks daily air quality, indicates how polluted the air is and the potential health effects on residents.
In Bangladesh, AQI measurements are based on five key pollutants: particulate matter (PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and ozone.
According to the World Health Organization, air pollution causes an estimated seven million deaths worldwide each year, primarily from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

Daughter’s dengue deteriorated rapidly without warning signs, physician parents realise too late
item.description:
Whenever patients sought advice on dengue, physician Muhammad Omar Faruq Raihan would instruct them to monitor closely for red flags: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or bleeding in vomit and stool. Yet, when his own daughter, Famiya Mashnur Rumaisa, contracted the virus, none of these typical warning signs manifested. Before her parents could even register that her condition was turning critical, the young girl passed away.

Famiya Mashnur was 8 years, 10 months, and 14 days old. She was a Class-III (English version) student at the Banasree branch of Ideal School in the capital. Her fever spiked on the morning of 29 September; within three days, on the afternoon of 1 October, she breathed her last.

Muhammad Omar Faruq Raihan works as an anaesthesia and ICU specialist at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery. His wife, Farzana Sultana, is an ophthalmologist at Vision Eye Hospital in Dhaka. Famiya was the couple’s elder daughter.

She had meticulously planned her upcoming birthday on 17 November—a trip to Cox’s Bazar to cut a cake and spend quality time with her parents and younger sister. She went shopping with her mother and bought matching outfits for herself and her younger sister.

“After she was found dengue positive in a test, there was no sign whatsoever that her condition was deteriorating,” physician Omar Faruq told Prothom Alo. “We simply couldn’t gauge it. Upon reaching Square Hospital, she couldn’t even survive half an hour in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) before passing away.”

The physician couple’s younger daughter, Farjin Mahnur Warisa, aged 5 years and 8 months, was constantly attached to her elder sister, who often bathed and took care of her. Unaware of the permanence of death, Farjin has been told that her sister—whom she affectionately called ‘Iya’—has gone to God, and she has processed the loss in her own innocent way.

Omar Faruq and Farzana Sultana recounted that on the night of Sunday, 27 September, Famiya complained of feeling feverish. Her temperature rose the following morning, preventing her from attending school. On Tuesday, diagnostic tests confirmed she was dengue-positive. An intravenous cannula was inserted at home to administer saline. As Omar Faruq had to travel outside Dhaka for urgent professional duties, no further blood tests were performed on Wednesday.

On Thursday morning, Famiya mentioned feeling unwell. Soon after, she suffered a sudden seizure and was rushed to a local hospital in Banasree. Lacking PICU facilities, she had to be transferred across the city to Square Hospital. Traffic delays compounded the critical situation; by the time they reached Square Hospital, her condition had severely worsened, and she began bleeding from her nose. Shortly after, she succumbed to the illness. Prior to this rapid decline, she had been alert, conversing with family members, and drinking coconut water sent by her grandmother.

Her mother, Farzana Sultana, now paces through their home, surrounded by memories of a daughter who loved organising her keepsakes. The grieving parents are attempting to find solace in the thought that her lifespan was destined to be short. Heartbreaking regrets linger—the girl had asked for mango juice the day before her death but could not drink it, and her birthday dress remains untouched in the wardrobe.

They cannot bring themselves to forget such memories: at this time last year, the whole family travelled together for Hajj, while the daughter took her last selfie with her parents and sister during a trip to Sajek in July.

Omar Faruq recalled his daughter’s sensitive nature, noting how she felt embarrassed when her mother changed her clothes in front of a domestic worker after a bout of vomiting.

He added that Famiya’s mother had also contracted dengue shortly before Famiya fell ill, but recovered with home care and IV saline. Unfortunately, those same interventions proved ineffective for their daughter.

Omar Faruq Raihan reflected that the outcome might have been different if adequate PICU facilities were available across hospitals, if public healthcare services were more robust, and if local authorities had initiated effective Aedes mosquito control measures ahead of the dengue season.

Pointing to an open waste dump near his Banasree residence where stagnant water accumulates, he noted that urban sanitation oversight remains severely neglected.

A specialist who daily treats severely burned children at the Burn Institute, Omar Faruq Raihan admitted he was always terrified that his daughter might hurt herself in the kitchen and repeatedly urged her to stay away from it. “In the end,” the grieving father lamented, “she suffered and died from the bite of a tiny mosquito.”

item.title: Lawyers scuffle at court over bail hearing of Maj (retd) Akhtaruzzaman
item.description:
During the hearing of Major (Retd.) Akhtaruzzaman’s bail application, BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami supporting lawyers got involved in an uproar and altercation in the presence of the judge.

This incident took place on Sunday afternoon in the court of Magistrate Jamshed Alam at Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Court.

During the tension between the two groups of lawyers, the judge entered his chamber but later returned to conduct the hearing. Even then, there were arguments and scuffles between the BNP and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers.

Following the unexpected situation in the courtroom, as Akhtaruzzaman was being brought down from the court building after the hearing, BNP and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers again engaged in a scuffle. Each side blamed the other for the incident.

Akhtaruzzaman was arrested by police on Friday last in a case regarding chaos at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka over a luggage and trolley crisis, obstruction to government work, and the accusation of assaulting an official.

After a one-day remand, he was presented in court on Sunday afternoon. The police sought an order to send him to jail, while Akhtaruzzaman’s lawyer applied for his bail.

Major (Retd.) Akhtaruzzaman, who was elected a Member of Parliament twice from BNP, joined Jamaat-e-Islami last December ahead of the 13th National Election.

A group of Jamaat-affiliated lawyers represented him in court today. Before the judge arrived at the bench, a dispute arose in the courtroom over space between pro-BNP lawyers and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers, leading to chaos and shoving between the two groups.

In this situation, the judge came to the bench at 2: 41 PM. Even after his arrival, the lawyers didn’t stop. The judge left the bench and went back to his chamber. When the situation calmed down a bit, the judge returned to the bench at 2: 45 PM.

At that time, Akhtaruzzaman, standing in the dock with his hand raised, requested permission from the judge, saying, "Ten lawyers will argue on my behalf. I am requesting permission for all ten to be heard."

During the hearing, there was again loud arguing and exchange of words between the two sides' lawyers in the presence of the judge.

Filing the application to keep Akhtaruzzaman detained in jail, the investigation officer of the case, Sub-Inspector Majedul Islam of the Airport Police Station, stated, during interrogation, the accused admitted to the truth of the incident and provided some information.

The obtained information from the accused is being verified. The investigation is ongoing comprehensively. In this situation, for the sake of a fair and unbiased investigation, it is imperative to keep the accused detained until the investigation is complete.

In the hearing, Akhtaruzzaman’s lawyer Abdur Razzak told the court, he (Akhtaruzzaman) is a former major and a several-time member of parliament. The allegations against him are false. This court granted permission for his interrogation yesterday. Today, after the remand, he has been brought to court. The allegation related to the airport incident is not his crime. As a conscious citizen, he has protested.

This lawyer argued that injustice and wrongdoing were done to Akhtaruzzaman at the airport, claiming many others also suffered from this hardship. Some of these incidents have been seen in videos on Facebook.

The conduct for which the case was filed was essentially his act of protest. Is protesting against injustice and wrongdoing a crime for a conscious citizen and a freedom fighter? As a freedom fighter, member of parliament, and former major, where everyone honours and respects him, injustice was done to him at the airport.

Claiming that Akhtaruzzaman was arrested for political reasons, his lawyer further told the court, "He is ill, suffering from various ailments. We are requesting his bail on any conditions. The sections submitted in the case are eligible for bail. We are requesting bail."

Meanwhile, another lawyer for the defence, Saifur Rahman, also applied for Akhtaruzzaman's bail.

Opposing the bail, the state lawyer Omar Farooq Farooqi told the court, "We have seen a video. In that, it seems this accused is behaving very badly at the airport. He is throwing items haphasardly. Protest is not a crime, but the language of protest should be like a protest. He did not protest there; he committed a crime. Assaulting someone can never be an expression of protest."

PP Omar Farooq further stated, "BNP has given birth to many leaders in this country. They forget after taking advantage. There are many such opportunists. They survived on our resources."

At this point, Jamaat-affiliated lawyers became agitated and protested. Akhtaruzzaman, standing in the accused dock, was seen smiling while looking at the PP and shaking his head to indicate 'no'.

The PP told the court, there can never be bail in this case. It is very necessary to know what power and support are behind such behaviour, for the sake of investigation. If the accused is granted bail, it will obstruct the investigation.

Protesting the prosecutor's statement, the defence lawyer Abdur Razzak said, "Yesterday, the PP called the accused 'discarded goods'. This cannot be a hearing. We protest."

At this stage of the hearing, at 3: 08 PM, lawyers of BNP and Jamaat-affiliated groups again caused an uproar. The judge then instructed them to stop.

At that time, the defence lawyers argued, "Considering age, physical condition, and illness, we are seeking the accused’s bail. This is a bailable case. He deserves bail." Objecting to this statement, the PP said, "Akhtaruzzaman has sided with the fascists and participated in illegal elections. He spoke against the July movement. To save himself after that, he joined Jamaat who have also sheltered him to give us slander. Jamaat fosters some people just for abusing the government, for questioning the government's development."

After hearing arguments from both sides, the court rejected the bail and ordered Akhtaruzzaman to be sent to jail.

After the court’s order, police, under strict security, escorted Akhtaruzzaman down the stairs. However, upon reaching the first floor, a noise and scuffle of BNP and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers were reported below the court building, and Akhtaruzzaman was held there for a moment.

At that time, BNP-supporting lawyers tried to disperse the Jamaat-affiliated lawyers and their supporters protesting below the court building. Both sides then got into a shoving and scuffling. Later, when police brought the situation under control, Akhtaruzzaman was brought down.

Later, in a briefing, the state's lawyer Omar Farooq Farooqi stated, "Jamaat wants to create mobs everywhere. That day, Akhtaruzzaman created a mob at the airport. Today, Jamaat's lawyers and their supporters from outside created a mob. Their intention is to worsen the situation by creating mobs. From the morning, I have seen them gathering. They had filled the courtroom beforehand."

On the other hand, Akhtaruzzaman's lawyer Abdur Razzak said, "What do they mean by outside people? We didn’t bring any outsiders. If every of the 35,000 lawyers have one client each, that makes 35,000 clients. What they are saying is not correct at all."
